subject: Business Law
notes: Legal core. No numerical questions apply; extra objective and case items included.

questions.text: An agreement enforceable by law is a
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A contract is an agreement that creates legal obligations.

questions.text: The minimum age at which a person can enter into a valid contract in India is
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Majority Act a person attains majority at eighteen.

questions.text: A proposal when accepted becomes a
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Acceptance of an offer converts the proposal into a promise.

questions.text: An agreement without consideration is always void
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: There are exceptions such as gifts and natural love and affection where consideration is not required.

questions.text: List the essential elements of a valid contract
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Offer and acceptance lawful consideration capacity free consent lawful object and certainty.
questions.explanation: These elements must all be present for a valid contract.

questions.text: Explain the modes of discharge of a contract
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: A contract is discharged by performance mutual agreement impossibility lapse of time operation of law and breach. Each brings the obligations to an end.
questions.explanation: Cover the various ways contractual obligations terminate.

questions.text: A contract to compensate a party for loss caused by another is a contract of
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Indemnity promises to make good a loss suffered by another.

questions.text: The person whose goods are delivered to another for a purpose on return is the
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: In bailment the bailor delivers goods to the bailee for a purpose on return.

questions.text: A contract of guarantee involves three parties
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Guarantee involves the creditor principal debtor and surety.

questions.text: Distinguish between indemnity and guarantee
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Indemnity involves two parties and one promise while guarantee involves three parties and a secondary liability of the surety.
questions.explanation: Guarantee has an extra party and a contingent liability.

questions.text: Explain the rights and duties of a bailee
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: A bailee must take reasonable care of the goods and return them as agreed and has the right to recover expenses and claim a lien for unpaid charges.
questions.explanation: Cover the duties of care and return and the rights of reimbursement.

questions.text: The Act that governs contracts for the sale of movable goods is the
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The Sale of Goods Act 1930 governs contracts for the sale of goods.

questions.text: The transfer of ownership of goods for a price is called a
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A sale transfers property in goods from seller to buyer for a price.

questions.text: In a contract of sale property in the goods passes immediately to the buyer
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: In a sale ownership passes at once while in an agreement to sell it passes later.

questions.text: Distinguish between a sale and an agreement to sell
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: In a sale property in goods transfers immediately while in an agreement to sell it transfers at a future time or on a condition.
questions.explanation: The timing of ownership transfer is the key difference.

questions.text: Explain the doctrine of caveat emptor and its exceptions
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Caveat emptor means let the buyer beware so the buyer must examine goods before purchase. Exceptions arise for fitness for purpose merchantable quality and sale by sample.
questions.explanation: State the rule then the exceptions protecting the buyer.

questions.text: A written promise to pay a fixed sum of money on demand is a
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A promissory note is an unconditional written promise to pay a fixed sum.

questions.text: A bill of exchange contains an order to pay whereas a promissory note contains a
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A bill orders payment while a note promises payment.

questions.text: A cheque is a bill of exchange drawn on a banker and payable on demand
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A cheque is a special bill of exchange drawn on a banker payable on demand.

questions.text: Define a negotiable instrument and list its types
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: A negotiable instrument is freely transferable by delivery and includes promissory notes bills of exchange and cheques.
questions.explanation: These instruments can pass from person to person freely.

questions.text: Explain the distinction between a bill of exchange and a cheque
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: A cheque is always drawn on a banker and payable on demand while a bill may be drawn on any person and may be payable after time. A cheque needs no acceptance but a bill usually requires it.
questions.explanation: Cover the drawee payable on demand and acceptance differences.

questions.text: A company is an artificial legal person created by
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A company is a legal person created by law distinct from its members.

questions.text: The document that defines the external objects and powers of a company is the
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The memorandum states the objects and scope of the company.

questions.text: A company has perpetual succession meaning its existence continues regardless of member changes
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Perpetual succession means the company continues despite changes in membership.

questions.text: State the characteristics of a company
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Separate legal entity perpetual succession limited liability common seal and transferable shares.
questions.explanation: These features distinguish a company from other forms of business.

questions.text: Explain the doctrine of separate legal entity with reference to a leading case
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: A company is distinct from its members as held in Salomon versus Salomon. Shareholders are not personally liable for company debts beyond their shares.
questions.explanation: Explain the corporate veil and the Salomon principle.

questions.text: The Act that protects consumers against unfair trade practices is the
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The Consumer Protection Act safeguards consumer rights and provides redressal.

questions.text: The three tier consumer dispute redressal machinery ends at the
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: District State and National Commissions form the three tiers.

questions.text: The Competition Act aims to prevent anti competitive agreements and abuse of dominance
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The Competition Act 2002 regulates anti competitive practices and combinations.

questions.text: List any four consumer rights
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Right to safety information choice to be heard and redressal.
questions.explanation: These rights protect consumers in the marketplace.

questions.text: Explain the objectives of the Consumer Protection Act
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: The Act protects consumers from unfair trade practices and defective goods and services and provides simple speedy and inexpensive redressal of grievances.
questions.explanation: Cover protection and the redressal machinery.

questions.text: Assertion: A minor cannot enter into a valid contract. Reason: The law presumes a minor lacks the capacity to contract
questions.subject: Business Law
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
questions.explanation: Incapacity of minors makes their agreements void ab initio.

questions.text: Match the instrument to its nature
questions.subject: Business Law
options: Promissory note - an order to pay
Bill of exchange - a promise to pay
questions.explanation: A cheque is drawn on a banker while a note is a promise and a bill is an order.

questions.text: Consent obtained by threatening harm is obtained by
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Coercion involves threats to obtain consent unlawfully.

questions.text: The person who is represented by an agent is called the
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The principal authorises the agent to act on his behalf.

questions.text: The Sale of Goods Act applies to immovable property
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The Act applies only to movable goods and not to immovable property.

questions.text: Explain the conditions and warranties in a contract of sale
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: A condition is essential to the contract and its breach allows repudiation while a warranty is collateral and its breach only allows damages.
questions.explanation: The remedy differs because conditions are more fundamental.

questions.text: Explain the types of companies under the Companies Act
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Companies may be classified by incorporation as chartered statutory or registered by liability as limited or unlimited and as private or public.
questions.explanation: Classify companies on the bases of incorporation liability and membership.

questions.text: Read the case: A offers to sell his car to B for 200000 but B replies accepting at 180000. Explain the legal position of Bs reply
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Bs reply is a counter offer which rejects the original offer. No contract is formed and B cannot later accept the original offer unless A renews it.
questions.explanation: A counter offer destroys the original offer.

questions.text: Read the case: A company sells a defective machine that injures a worker despite a disclaimer in the contract. Explain whether the consumer can claim under consumer law
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: The consumer can claim for a defective product and unfair practice as the right to safety and redressal cannot be excluded by a disclaimer under the Consumer Protection Act.
questions.explanation: Statutory consumer rights override contractual disclaimers.

questions.text: The concept of a company having a personality distinct from its members is called
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: The corporate veil separates the company from its shareholders.

questions.text: Explain the concept of free consent and the factors vitiating it
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Free consent means agreeing without coercion undue influence fraud misrepresentation or mistake. Any of these factors makes consent not free and may make the contract voidable.
questions.explanation: Cover each vitiating factor and its effect on the contract.

questions.text: A contract entered into by an agent within authority binds the principal
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: An agent acting within authority binds the principal to third parties.

questions.text: Explain the rights of an unpaid seller
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: An unpaid seller has rights against the goods including lien stoppage in transit and resale and rights against the buyer for the price and damages.
questions.explanation: Distinguish rights against goods from rights against the buyer.

questions.text: Define consideration and state its legal rules
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Consideration is something of value given in return for a promise and must be real lawful and need not be adequate.
questions.explanation: Consideration must move at the desire of the promisor and be lawful.

questions.text: Explain the procedure for the incorporation of a company
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Incorporation requires filing the memorandum and articles with the registrar paying fees and obtaining the certificate of incorporation which gives the company legal existence.
questions.explanation: Trace the steps from documents to the certificate of incorporation.

questions.text: The winding up of a company brings its existence to an end
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: Winding up liquidates assets and ends the companys existence.

questions.text: Explain the meaning and kinds of agency
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Agency is the relationship where an agent acts for a principal. It may arise by express or implied agreement ratification or necessity.
questions.explanation: Describe the modes by which agency is created.

questions.text: A bill of exchange that is payable at sight is called a demand bill
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.explanation: A demand bill is payable immediately on presentation.

questions.text: Explain the remedies available to a consumer under the Consumer Protection Act
questions.subject: Business Law
questions.correctAnswer: Consumers may seek removal of defects replacement refund of price compensation and cessation of unfair practices through the district state or national commissions.
questions.explanation: Cover the remedies and the redressal forums.
